definition: Neural induction is the stage in a stem-cell developmental protocol when cells are guided to become neural progenitors, the early cells that give rise to brain and nervous system tissue. In this packet, a longer neural induction period produced midbrain neural progenitors with different receptor expression than a shorter protocol.

reasons: The packet does not define “neural induction” as a stage that guides stem cells to become neural progenitors, nor does it state that these early cells give rise to brain and nervous system tissue.

The packet only supports that “a longer neural induction and regional patterning period” increases expression of OPRM1 (mu) and OPRK1 (kappa) in midbrain neural progenitors compared to a shorter protocol, rather than supporting the broader characterization about neural induction in general.

The packet does not support the specific claim that a longer neural induction period produced midbrain neural progenitors with “different receptor expression” in the general terms used; it only provides receptor-expression results (OPRM1/OPRK1) for that longer vs shorter period.

The definition adds unsupported general biology (“cells guided to become neural progenitors, the early cells that give rise to brain and nervous system tissue”); the packet only shows a longer neural induction and regional patterning period in an iPSC-based midbrain neural progenitor model.

The packet supports that a longer neural induction period was compared with a shorter protocol and affected receptor expression, but it does not define neural induction itself as a stem-cell developmental stage that produces neural progenitors.
